newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Mideast and African port conditions - Lloyds.
newsitem.headline: Mideast and African port conditions - Lloyds.

text.p: Port conditions from Lloyds Shipping Intelligence Service --

ANGOLA, Feb 10 - Luanda - Quay congestion is a continuing problem and clearance of cargo continues to take a considerable time. Lack of space on quays is slowing discharging operations. At present, all berths are occupied and 4 vessels are waiting for general cargo berths. Current delays 2-5 days, dependent on vessel type and cargo. Lobito, Namibe - No delays reported. Cabinda - Discharging operations offshore to lighters. No delays reported.

ISRAEL, Feb 11 - Haifa - No labour problems. Six vessels discharging at berth (5 general cargo, 1 bulker), 4 container vessels, 1 tanker. 3 Bulkers waiting at anchorage to discharge, 1 container vessel, 1 tanker. 1 Vessel under repair/dry-docked, 3 awaiting orders, 7 due with 2-3 days delay expected. Ashdod - no labour problems. 12 Vessels discharging at berth (10 general cargo, 2 bulkers). 2 Bulkers loading at berth, 4 container vessels, 4 general cargo vessels waiting at anchorage to discharge, 1 bulker waiting to load, 2 container vessels. 2-4 Days delay expected. Eilat - One bulker loading at berth, 1 passenger vessel, 1 vessel due.

MOZAMBIQUE, Feb 11 - Nacala - Port working normally. No restrictions on berthing and sailing during night time. Draft restrictions, 9.5 metres at general cargo berths and 14 metres at container berths. One tug available. Beira - General cargo berths, working normally. Container terminal/other terminals - Working normally, 24 hour berthing/sailing for vessels up to 140 metres loa. Some restrictions for larger vessels and subject to prior arrangements with port captain. Maximum draft for 24 hour navigation 7.5 metres. Two tugs available. Maputo - 24 Hour berthing/sailing for vessels up to 120 metres loa. Some restrictions for larger vessels and subject to prior arrangements with port captain. All berths working normally and expected to remain so. Draft restriction in the channel is 9.0 metres less 0.5 metres (ukc) plus the rise of tide. Maximum draft for 24 hour navigation is 9 metres.
NAMIBIA, Feb 11 - Walvis Bay - Port working normally.

SOUTH AFRICA, Feb 11 - Richards Bay - General cargo berths - Congested at present, with 48 hours berthing delay expected from 10-17/2. Bulk import berths - Vessels can berth on arrival from 10-17/2. Bulk export berths (minerals etc.) - Congested at present, with 12-24 hours berthing delay. From 13-17/2 congestion will be alleviated and vessels expected to be able to berth on arrival. Bulk coal berths - At present 4 vessels are berthed, 10 at anchorage, 21 due up to and including 17/2. Berthing delays of approx. 4 days experienced at present.

Durban - Container terminal - Some vessels experiencing delays whilst others berthing on arrival. Point, New pier, Maydon wharf berths - Working normally for general cargo vessels. However, port under pressure with a large number of attached vessels, some of which are fully laden and require deep-water berths. Maize terminal (Maydon wharf 8) - One maize loader expected for Feb. Bunker supplies - Product available but this could change daily due to bunching of vessels. Dry-dock/floating dock - Fully booked until the end of March.

East London - General cargo, combi terminal berths - Very busy, but no delays expected at this stage. Port Elizabeth - Working normally with no delays expected on any berths. Cape Town - Container terminal - Approx. 24 hours of working time lost over the past weekend due to south easterly winds. All berths occupied at present with vessels operating, but further winds/delays can be expected. Numerous vessels due this week which, weather permitting, are expected to berth/operate on arrival. Breakbulk,general cargo berths - Working normally, with vessels berthing/operating on arrival and no delays expected. Fruit berths - Presently fully occupied with deciduous loaders and another five vessels due this week. Bunker berths - Working normally, no delays expected. Dry-docks and repair quays - Fully booked until the end of May. For dates after that it is essential that early booking is made. Saldanha Bay - Port working normally.

TUNISIA, Feb 7 - Sousse - Four vessels in port of which 1 awaiting orders, 1 discharging pvc, 1 loading vegetable oil, 1 discharging cotton. Tunis - Three vessels discharging (1 marble blocks, 1 paper in reels, 1 steel coils), 1 general cargo vessel, 1 vessel awaiting instructions, 2 under arrest. Rades - Four ro-ro vessels. La Goulette - North side - 1 Vessel discharging cars/pvc, 1 passenger vessel, 1 general cargo, 1 tanker discharging soya. South side - 1 Vessel discharging grain, 1 loading clinker, 2 vessels in roads. Gabes - Feb 8 - No labour problems. One acid tanker loading at berth, 3 vessels discharging at berth (2 bulk sulphur, 1 bulk barley), 1 vessel waiting at anchor to discharge bagged talc.

UNITED ARAB EMIRATES, Feb 2-8 - Dubai - 183 Vessels of which 82 containers, 10 general cargo, 1 general cargo/containers, 4 bulk carriers, 4 car carriers, 12 tankers, 4 naval vessels, 3 UAE naval vessels, 2 livestock carriers, 3 bunkering/under repair/taking stores etc., 3 dhows, 13 barges, 13 tugs, 23 supply boats, 5 lpg vessels, 1 survey vessel. 5 Vessels discharging at berth (2 containers, 1 general cargo, 2 tankers). 7 Vessels under repair/laid-up (1 general cargo, 6 tankers). 34 Vessels due of which 25 containers, 7 general cargo, 2 tankers, no delays expected.
